observations: Blue and white electric steam iron.
Brand name 'Sonik' is printed on the side in red text.
The iron has a braided power cord.
The soleplate has multiple steam vents.
Top-mounted buttons for water spray and steam burst are visible.
A technical specification sticker is on the base but the text is blurry.
Photo 1 shows the end of the cord which appears to be a standard AC plug, not a USB connector.

claims.evidence: The exterior appears clean in photos, but internal condition and 'as new' status cannot be confirmed.
Photos 0, 1, and 2 show a thick, braided AC power cord. Steam irons of this type require high voltage and do not use USB charging cables.

risks.risk: The heating element may be burnt out or non-functional.
risks.proof: A video showing the iron plugged into a wall outlet and successfully heating up.

risks.risk: The water tank or internal seals may leak when pressurized.
risks.proof: A video of the iron filled with water, heated, and used to produce steam without leaking from the body.

risks.risk: The soleplate may have scratches or a damaged non-stick coating not visible in the low-resolution shots.
risks.proof: A clear, high-resolution close-up of the entire soleplate.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the specification sticker on the base to identify the model number.
Video of the iron plugged in, heating up, and emitting steam.
Clear photo of the power plug at the end of the cord.
Close-up photo of the soleplate surface.
response.reason: The item is clearly a Sonik brand steam iron. Although the seller's claim regarding a USB cable is incorrect and suggests a lack of knowledge or a template error, the physical item is identifiable and can be priced at its worst-case functional state.
